title: Capacity forensics and adaptive burst safeguards after tiered-latency spike
creator: Rhea Patel
description:
Summary:
During a multi-tenant dedicated-cluster event on 2026-02-16 we observed a cascade of tail-latency regressions affecting three customers. The immediate trigger was a sustained increase in short-running high-QPS jobs from a single tenant that temporarily exhausted the soft reservation budget and caused aggressive eviction & slow rehydration of KV caches. Existing burst tokens allowed the tenant to consume capacity above its configured reservation for >18 minutes; autoscaling did not react due to scheduling/placement edge cases and token buckets not decaying fast enough between burst windows.

Scope of this ticket:
1) capture the forensic findings and create reproducible test cases that model the tenant behavior;
2) deliver short-term operational mitigations (admission controls, emergency reservation bump playbook);
3) implement a medium-term adaptive burst safeguard and reservation-sizing feedback loop;
4) update runbooks, SLOs, and customer communications templates.

Key findings (forensic highlights):
- The noisy tenant pattern was characterized by ~200ms bursts of 1k small requests over ~30s windows repeated every 90s, which defeats simple exponential decay burst token implementations.
- Reservation estimator used a 5-min percentile window; this smoothed over bursty patterns and under-provisioned for tail bursts.
- Kernel scheduling decisions at the node allocator occasionally co-located eviction-sensitive tenants with the noisy tenant due to affinity rules not considering recent burst score.
- KV cache rehydration penalty amplified the latency because evicted cache entries for overlapped models required token-level recomputation that serialized on a hot lock.

Outcome goals:
- Prevent a single tenant from causing >10% tail-latency regression for co-tenants across a node within 5 minutes of onset.
- Provide operators an automated safety-rail that can temporarily limit burst allowance for tenants exhibiting pathological patterns while keeping functional throughput for healthy tenants.
- Surface precise telemetry so PMs/SREs can decide reservation adjustments and billing reconciliation if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Forensics: reproducible load generator script checked in that replicates the tenant burst pattern
Mitigation: admission controller rule to cap sustained burst rate with rollout to canary cluster
Adaptive burst: implement moving-average burst-decay algorithm and new token bucket config with tests
Telemetry: new metrics (tenant_burst_score, reservation_shortfall, kv_rehydrate_time) emitted to metrics back-end
Runbook: updated dedicated-capacity runbook with emergency reservation bump and rollback steps
Operational test: synthetic tenants exercise the canary policy and show <10% tail-latency impact in 90% of runs
